title: Customer IaC profile patterns for VPC tailoring and safe upgrade orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and prototype a repeatable pattern for customer-specific Terraform composition that supports per-customer network customizations, safe automated upgrades, and integrated runtime health checks. The goal is a documented minimal API (module + variables + patching rules) that platform engineers and customer SREs can use without forking core modules. This ticket covers design decisions, a reference implementation, CI upgrade hooks, and validation e2e tests across three pilot customers.
acceptance_criteria: Reference repo (redwood/customer-iac-profiles) contains: base modules, a recommended directory layout, and three customer profile examples that compile with terraform 1.5+
Upgrade pipeline demonstrates a canary rollout to 1 of 3 customers, with automatic plan generation, human approval gate, and rollback path
redwood_healthcheck Terraform module included and wired into outputs for Private deployments; healthcheck emits pass/fail via CloudWatch/Datadog metric or a remote-state flag
Documentation (CONTRIBUTING.md + pattern guide) lists variable precedence, safe patching methods, and CI steps for customers to opt-in/out
E2E smoke tests run in CI that validate: plan/apply success, drift detection on a seeded change, and healthcheck failure detection triggers alerting runbook
decisions: Prefer composition + overlay patches over per-customer forks to minimize divergence and simplify upgrades
Adopt a three-layer precedence model: core modules (redwood/*) < tenant_profile (customer-controlled) < env_overrides (ops-controlled)
Use provider aliasing and explicit provider injection in modules so customer networking / vpc providers can be swapped without module changes
Expose a small surface of 'extension points' (locals-based merge hooks and module wrapper interfaces) instead of allowing arbitrary resource overrides inside core modules
Implement upgrade orchestration outside Terraform apply (CI orchestrator) to avoid embedding complex lifecycle logic inside modules; Terraform run is the atomic operation invoked by the orchestrator
implementation_notes: Directory pattern: /profiles/<customer>/main.tf imports redwood modules and defines tenant_profile.tfvars; avoid editing redwood modules directly
Patching pattern: supply a tenant_local variable map and use merge(local.base, var.tenant_local) in module inputs to enable targeted per-customer changes
Avoid using null_resource for permanent production hooks; use a dedicated redwood_maintenance resource (stateless) that maps to CI checks and external orchestration via remote state triggers
Remote state: per-customer remote state backends (S3+lock) to prevent cross-tenant plan/application interference, with IAM roles scoped to customer teams

Upgrade flow: 1) tag module release (git) 2) CI generates terraform plan per-profile 3) canary apply to non-production customer 4) gather healthchecks + metrics for 30m 5) rollout with staggered batch applies + automated rollback on regressions
Healthchecks: redwood_healthcheck module provides optional probes (api-gateway probe, internal readiness endpoint, kv-cache validation) and writes a summary key to remote state/monitoring
Testing: use terratest and a lightweight emulated network harness for fast smoke validation; full e2e runs scheduled nightly for each customer profile
Secrets: require use of customer KMS/secret-backend and never include secrets in profile repos; provide example secret references in docs
Policy-as-code: integrate OPA/Conftest checks in CI to catch disallowed patterns (e.g., broad CIDR changes) before apply

notes: Trade-offs: composition reduces duplication but requires well-designed extension points; over-exposing hooks increases maintenance burden

We intentionally avoid recommending Terragrunt as the only supported approach — it can be useful for labs/proof-of-concept but core pattern should be plain Terraform module composition so customers without Terragrunt can adopt
Observed anti-pattern in audits: customers committing provider blocks in profiles; mitigation: provider aliasing examples and CI linting rule
